inspection_summary: Inspected all 930 normalized lines, including prose, displayed formulas, page boundaries, references, and the three figure captions. The source contains three distinct proposal layers: an approximate SUSY inverse-spectral construction, a theta/Mellin map that reformulates zeta zeros as orthogonality-like relations, and a continuum fractal-string duality. Its strongest reusable content is in the explicit constructions, equivalences, and failure analysis; the authors themselves state that the SUSY amplitudes are approximate, that the scalar product interpretation is not rigorous and is replaced by a complex-valued map, that generic off-critical zeros cannot be excluded by the permutation analysis, and that the later RH conclusion is conditional on an unproved symmetry or parameter-independence assertion. Formula extraction is mostly recoverable from adjacent prose, but exact displayed expressions remain scan-dependent.

sections_inspected.label: Title, abstract, and source front matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies the three proposed spectral, orthogonality, and fractal-string routes and their claimed relation to RH.

sections_inspected.label: 1 Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates Hilbert-Polya, random-matrix statistics, p-adic oscillators, and the prior non-Hermitian orthogonality proposal; also outlines the paper.

sections_inspected.label: 2 A supersymmetric potential
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds an antisymmetric p-adic SUSY potential and poses an inverse eigenvalue system, while delimiting its shape-invariance and approximation limitations.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Operator, theta potential, and zeta-valued pairing
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the first-order operator family and theta-series potential, derives the completed-zeta pairing, specializes parameters, and replaces the invalid Hilbert-space interpretation by a complex map.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Orthogonality reformulations and interference
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates critical-line zeta zeros to orthogonality-like relations, reduces arbitrary pairings to a reference-state pairing, and interprets symmetric-state interference.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Symmetry audit, obstruction, and conditional theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Enumerates symmetry mappings, exposes why most do not exclude generic off-line zeros, and isolates the additional double-reflection invariance needed for the conditional conclusion.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Parameter-family reformulation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recasts the claim as parameter-independent orthogonality across a continuous operator family and invokes discreteness of zeros; ends with a summary of conditional results.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Discrete fractal-string setup
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces geometric and frequency counting functions, their zeta factorization, pole-based complex dimensions, and a Cantor-string example.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Continuum Riemann fractal string and dual
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proposes complex continuum length, frequency, and measure data whose counting-function ratio is zeta, then defines an RFS through poles at zeta zeros.

sections_inspected.label: 5 Conclusions and acknowledgements
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Offers speculative multifractal analogies and records that an earlier theorem-3 argument contained a vicious circle; no new completed mechanism is developed.

sections_inspected.label: Figures 1-3 and captions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Visually illustrates orthogonal-state patterns, the doubly infinite family, and the inner/outer reflection rectangles; captions provide usable support while plot bodies are layout-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Approximate p-adic SUSY inverse eigenvalue system
accepted_units.why_material: Turns the Hilbert-Polya wish for a Hermitian spectrum into a concrete inverse problem: choose an antisymmetric prime-harmonic SUSY potential and solve quantization plus turning-point constraints for amplitudes and orbit endpoints from prescribed zeta-zero ordinates. The source also marks the decisive limitation that the phase-integral condition is exact only for shape-invariant potentials, so the recovered amplitudes are merely approximate here.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 unit retained at its original span. It begins at the section heading, contains its own Hilbert-Polya motivation and all stated constraints, and ends with the transition to the separate direct-orthogonality proposal.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (1)-(4), product/sum indexing, and the phase integral are essential. The prose recovers the inverse-problem architecture, but exact symbols and the apparent duplicated partner-Hamiltonian sign should be scan-verified before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Scale-covariant first-order operator generated by a theta-series potential
accepted_units.why_material: Defines a non-self-adjoint first-order operator with explicit eigenfunctions, a partner operator, and a potential chosen so its exponential is a Jacobi theta series. This is the representation change that makes a spectral-looking state construction analytically connect to zeta through Mellin integration.
accepted_units.context_note: Read with the following pairing unit; this span supplies the operator, eigenfunctions, theta choice, and scale covariance rather than a self-adjoint Hilbert-Polya realization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (5)-(9) determine signs, exponents, and the theta-series parameter. Prose makes the construction legible, but the extracted superscripts and summation exponent should be checked against the page image for exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Mellin pairing converts state pairs into the completed zeta function
accepted_units.why_material: Combines the completed-zeta functional equation, the scale-invariant measure, the theta Mellin representation, and a change of variables to express a two-state pairing as a transformed completed zeta value. The discrete parameter transformation and relation between k and l expose how zeta reflection symmetry is encoded in the operator family.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit establishes the analytic bridge but not a positive-definite inner product or a proof of RH. Its output is interpreted cautiously in the next unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (10)-(13), conjugation in the combined state parameter, and the affine zeta argument are indispensable. The derivation is prose-supported, but exact factors of 2 and l are formula-image sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Critical-strip normalization and replacement of the scalar product by a complex map
accepted_units.why_material: Derives that the proposed norm depends only on the real part, fixes a sign convention on the critical line, then directly confronts the failure of the Hilbert-space scalar-product interpretation. Replacing the integral by a map from two complex labels to a completed-zeta value is a crucial semantic downgrade that prevents orthogonality language from silently carrying positivity or Hermiticity.
accepted_units.context_note: Overlaps the opening of the carried v1 orthogonality unit because lines 302-314 are the explicit caveat required to interpret all subsequent uses of orthogonality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium-high: the affine norm formula and map S are displayed formulas, but the limitation and replacement are explicit in prose. Exact map arguments should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Reference-state reduction of zeta zeros to orthogonality-like relations
accepted_units.why_material: After disclaiming a rigorous scalar-product interpretation, specializes the complex map and proves algebraic orthogonality relations for symmetric state labels. It then shows that every pairwise map evaluation can be rewritten against the reference state, yielding an exact equivalence between a zeta zero and vanishing of that reference-state map.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 unit retained at its original span. It requires the bounded preceding operator, theta/Mellin, parameter, and non-Hilbert-map setup recorded in v1_context_repairs; without that context the word orthogonal overstates the construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (15)-(17), complex conjugation, and affine label transformations are essential. The prose preserves the logical direction, but exact formula arguments should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Zeros as destructive interference for reflected state labels
accepted_units.why_material: Forms a superposition of labels s and 1-s and observes that cross terms vanish exactly at critical-line zero ordinates, giving a Pythagorean-style additivity of the map-defined norm. This supplies a distinct physical interpretation of the same vanishing relation and explicitly locates the destructive-interference lines.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an interpretation inside the complex-map formalism, not evidence that the states inhabit a positive Hilbert space; inherit the caveat at lines 292-314.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium-high: equations (18)-(19) establish the superposition and conjugate cross terms, while the surrounding prose recovers the interpretation.

accepted_units.title: Permutation audit fails to exclude generic off-critical zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Systematically compares the four reflected zero locations with four reference-state orthogonality arguments. It rejects permutations that smuggle in the RH through s*=1-s, classifies generic and degenerate mappings, and concludes that generic off-critical orthogonal states cannot be discarded. This negative result is the paper's clearest protection against a circular symmetry proof.
accepted_units.context_note: Figure 3 at lines 919-925 supports the rectangle geometry, but the classification and failure conclusion are stated in prose here and do not require the plot body.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: affine complex labels and the 24-permutation count matter, but the cases and obstruction are recoverable from prose. The rectangle visualization is helpful rather than essential.

accepted_units.title: Double-reflection covariance criterion for affine zeta maps
accepted_units.why_material: Isolates an exact affine constraint, 2b+a=1, under which the map from state labels to zeta arguments commutes with both conjugation and reflection. It makes explicit that the claimed RH consequence assumes the orthogonal states possess the double-reflection symmetry; the theorem does not establish that assumption.
accepted_units.context_note: Begins with the transition from the failed generic analysis and ends at the source's own conditional statement. It must be paired with the preceding obstruction to avoid presenting a conditional criterion as an unconditional proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the affine equations are concise and prose-explained; exact coefficient substitutions for k and l remain formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Continuous operator-family deformation turns RH into parameter-independent orthogonality
accepted_units.why_material: Parametrizes a family of operators satisfying the reflection constraint, reformulates RH as independence of reference-state orthogonality from the family parameter, and argues that a continuously moving real part is incompatible with a discrete zero set unless the fixed point is one half. This exposes both the intended deformation mechanism and its unproved premise.
accepted_units.context_note: The statement labeled (i), rather than discreteness alone, supplies the needed parameter-independence assumption. Lines 505-515 merely summarize this and the earlier results.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: affine relations among s, s-prime, a, b, k, and l carry the argument. Prose is sufficient for the conceptual move, but exact subscripts and coefficients should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Fractal-string frequency spectrum factors through the Riemann zeta function
accepted_units.why_material: Separates a string's geometric length counting function from the integer harmonics of each length and derives the reusable factorization ZF=ZL times zeta. It also explains why poles of the geometric factor encode complex dimensions and why collisions with zeta zeros affect spectral visibility.
accepted_units.context_note: The surrounding physical examples are motivational; the reusable mechanism is the separation of primitive lengths from harmonic multiplicities and its Dirichlet-series factorization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (21)-(24) define the counting functions and factorization. The prose makes the sums' roles clear, but exact domains and exponents should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Cantor-string poles generate complex dimensions
accepted_units.why_material: Works from length multiplicities and scaling ratios to a geometric counting series whose poles have a real part equal to Cantor dimension and periodically spaced imaginary parts. This is the concrete model motivating pole-defined complex dimensions in the proposed Riemann fractal string.
accepted_units.context_note: The final quantum-gravity remark is speculative; the accepted mechanism is the counting-series-to-poles calculation and its dimensional interpretation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the OCR around equation (25) is crowded, although the prose clearly states lengths, degeneracies, pole equation, and resulting real and imaginary parts. Scan verification is required for exact algebra.

accepted_units.title: Continuum fractal-string duality encodes zeta as a ratio of counting integrals
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces discrete lengths and frequencies by complex-valued continuum maps and measures for a string and its dual, proposes their counting-integral ratio as zeta, and defines a Riemann fractal string by poles of its geometric counting function at zeta zeros. It is the source's explicit attempt to realize the functional equation as duality between representations.
accepted_units.context_note: The text says suitable fractal pseudo-measures and renormalized contour tools could define the integrals only in principle; it does not construct functions satisfying all asserted properties or prove the duality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (27)-(29), tilded dual data, measures, and the zero-versus-pole alternative are central. Extraction is prose-recoverable at the conceptual level, but exact integrals and conjugacy claims need scan verification.

v1_context_repairs.reason: The carried span begins inside the method's caveat and otherwise lacks the D1 eigenfunctions, theta-series choice, Mellin-to-Z derivation, k=1 and l=4 specialization, and explicit replacement of a non-rigorous scalar product by the map S. Those lines are necessary to interpret its orthogonality claims without importing Hilbert-space properties.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Two inverse directions toward a spectral RH representation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source contrasts fitting a SUSY potential to prescribed zero ordinates with designing an operator/theta representation whose pairings evaluate the completed zeta; together they expose inverse spectral fitting versus analytic representation as different Hilbert-Polya moves.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The first is approximate and presupposes ordinates, while the second is non-self-adjoint and does not produce a positive Hilbert-space inner product.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Vanishing-map reformulation checked by its own obstruction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The exact reference-state vanishing equivalence is mathematically separable from the stronger claim that such vanishing forces the critical line, and the permutation audit demonstrates the missing exclusion of generic off-line cases.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This synthesis validates a reformulation and a failure diagnosis, not RH or the existence of a suitable Hilbert-Polya operator.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Reflection covariance, deformation, and the fixed line
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Affine covariance under conjugation and reflection gives a fixed point at one half, while continuous parameter deformation plus a discrete target spectrum motivates pinning the real part to that fixed point.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The decisive double-reflection symmetry or parameter-independent orthogonality is assumed rather than derived, so discreteness cannot complete the argument alone.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Discrete factorization to continuum dual string
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The discrete separation of lengths from integer harmonics explains zeta factorization, the Cantor example explains pole-defined complex dimensions, and the continuum proposal tries to lift both ideas into a string/dual-string realization of zeta reflection.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The required complex continuum data and pseudo-measures are proposed only in principle, and the source does not establish their existence, uniqueness, analytic domains, or functional-equation duality.

within_source_saturation: Saturated at the level of distinct source-supported mechanisms and limitations: the SUSY inverse problem, theta/Mellin map, map-versus-inner-product caveat, zero/orthogonality equivalence, interference reading, generic-symmetry obstruction, conditional reflection/deformation criterion, discrete fractal-string factorization, Cantor pole example, and continuum dual proposal are each represented. Remaining prose is recap, speculation, bibliography, page furniture, or figure layout whose useful captions have been accounted for.
